text:
Alex K: hey @Maria (People Ops) quick q — planning to be away from my home base (CA) for ~6 months next spring (writing retreat + travel). Am I still eligible for the WFH stipend? any tax/payroll stuff I should worry about?
Maria (People Ops): thanks for the heads up, Alex. can you share exact dates + countries? short trips are easier, but 6 months is long enough to trigger payroll/tax rules in a few places.
Alex K: rough plan is Apr 1 -> Sep 30, split between Portugal (4 months) and back to US for the rest.
Maria (People Ops): ok — that helps. high-level: for international stays >90 days we usually need to treat payroll/benefits differently (potential local employer obligations). please start by filing the remote-stay form: https://intranet.redwood/ops/remote-stay-form and attach passport + address proof for Portugal.
Dave (Payroll): +1. if you're on US payroll and will be tax resident in PT for a portion of the year, we may need to onboard via our EOR partner or set up local payroll there. also depends on visa type. 6 months could create tax residency in PT (check 183-day rule). please don't change your home address until payroll team confirms the path.
Sophie (Finance): regarding the WFH stipend — we usually continue pro-rated stipend while on approved temporary remote overseas, but if payroll switches to local entity, stipend treatment may change (might be a local allowance or combined into net pay). also note currency/payment and withholding differences.
Alex K: understood. what about benefits (healthcare) — will I be covered while abroad?
Maria (People Ops): short answer: it depends. EU stays often require local health coverage; our US medical plan may not cover long-term stays abroad. Benefits team will review after payroll confirms employment entity. can you cc people-ops@redwood with the form so we can loop benefits + legal?
Dave (Payroll): next steps from payroll side: 1) submit remote-stay form, 2) payroll will run a country impact assessment (~3–5 business days), 3) if local payroll required we'll send onboarding docs (ID + local bank info generally), 4) timing: need 2–4 weeks lead time before your first day abroad.
Alex K: got it. for the WFH stipend amount — is it the same while abroad?
Sophie (Finance): usually same monthly amount while on approved temporary remote status, but we'll confirm once payroll flags any local payroll changes.
Maria (People Ops): one more note — if you're planning to be truly nomadic (no fixed address) that complicates things for tax residency and benefits. if you can provide a primary address in Portugal for the period that helps.
Alex K: thanks — filing the form now. will attach dates and passport.
PayrollBot: Remote stay form received for Alex K (ID: RS-1842101123). People Ops and Payroll notified.
Dave (Payroll): received the form — we'll kick off the country assessment and post back here with recommended path by EOD Friday.
Alex K: perfect, appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
